class.name: DirectionalBulletsData2D
class.description: Ensure that the [member MultiMeshBulletsData2D.transforms] and [member all_bullet_speed_data] are set, otherwise spawning fails with an error and no bullets are created (missing speed data falls back to zeros). Check [MultiMeshBulletsData2D]'s documentation for the rest of the properties.

members.member: If enabled, the bullets will adjust their direction when rotating, instead of only spinning in place.

[b]MANDATORY[/b] You can provide [BulletSpeedData2D] for every single bullet - meaning that it should contain the same amount of data as the [member MultiMeshBulletsData2D.transforms].
Warning: If you provide less [BulletSpeedData2D] than the amount of bullets (same as amount of transforms), ALL bullets will use only the first provided speed data. Note: [BulletSpeedData2D] has a helper static method that you can use to generate random speed data - [method BulletSpeedData2D.generate_random_data()].
Shared curves applied to every bullet at spawn time (and on pool reuse). Tick precedence is unchanged: shared channels win ties, per-bullet curves fill gaps, plain speed data covers the rest.

Shared rotation applied to every bullet at spawn time (and on pool reuse), taking precedence over per-bullet rotation data when set. Null (default) disables the feature and the rotation array drives instead.

Shared speed applied to every bullet at spawn time (and on pool reuse), taking precedence over [member all_bullet_speed_data] when set. Null (default) disables the feature and the array drives instead. Note: shared movement-speed curves still outrank it per tick.
Whether the shared movement pattern rotates bullets to face their direction of travel.

Path to a [Path2D] in the scene tree whose curve is applied as the movement pattern of every bullet at spawn time (and on pool reuse). Resolved relative to the [BulletFactory2D] with a scene-root fallback; absolute paths always work. Empty (default) disables the feature.
Whether the shared movement pattern repeats instead of stopping at the end of the curve.
